arguments.value: 25-year-old previously healthy woman transferred to ICU after abrupt collapse with fever, encephalopathy, rash/purpura, severe thrombocytopenia, acute liver and renal failure, and shock with multiorgan dysfunction. Extensive infectious and autoimmune workup was initially negative; empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics and supportive care were started. Leptospirosis was later confirmed by positive IgM after a history of spring water exposure/endemic residence, with MRI showing meningoencephalitis/hypoxic-ischemic injury. Course was complicated by prolonged ventilation and recurrent MDR Pseudomonas/Acinetobacter bloodstream and respiratory infections, and she died of multiorgan failure two months later.
